target.title: Add deep regression review prototype
target.body:
Closes #439.

## TLDR

- Adds a default-off OpenClaw deep-regression review prototype for high-risk PRs.
- GitNexus is optional and advisory. GitHub diff/checkout context remains authoritative.
- The latest ClawSweeper code finding is fixed: review caching now uses stable graph-content state instead of a packet hash that changes with `generatedAt`.
- Maintainer-boundary concerns are now committed as repo documentation in `docs/deep-regression-review.md` instead of living only in PR prose.
- No 1M-context or release-safety claim is made. Context-window size is telemetry only.

Current head: `c96a27278952481a20ebb22538c5b0b2173d088a`

## What Changed

- Adds deterministic OpenClaw high-risk classification for core/runtime/auth/session/security/provider-routing/release/config surfaces.
- Adds an optional GitNexus advisory context packet behind `CLAWSWEEPER_GITNEXUS_CONTEXT=1`.
- Adds packet freshness, exact packet SHA, stable content SHA, byte budget, omitted-context accounting, redaction hash, and fail-closed behavior for secret-like output.
- Extends the decision schema, prompt contract, report frontmatter, public rendering, and close gating with `deepRegressionReview`.
- Adds context-window telemetry via `CLAWSWEEPER_EXPECTED_CONTEXT_WINDOW_TOKENS`; unknown stays `unknown`.
- Adds review-cache safety so graph-context changes bust cached reports, while identical graph context generated at different times can reuse prior review content.
- Adds command-status cleanup so repeated `@clawsweeper re-review` commands do not leave stale ClawSweeper status comments for older heads.
- Adds maintainer-facing documentation: `docs/deep-regression-review.md`.

## ClawSweeper Findings Addressed

ClawSweeper used several `[P1]` labels across proof guidance, risk notes, and maintainer options. The actual current-head code finding was the stable GitNexus cache-state issue. This PR now addresses each bucket as follows:

| ClawSweeper item | Resolution |
| --- | --- |
| Stable GitNexus cache key | Fixed in code. `GitNexusContextPacket` now has `contentSha256`, which excludes run-local packet telemetry such as `generatedAt`; review cache state uses `contentSha256`. |
| Regression coverage for cache reuse | Added tests proving packet SHA changes across timestamps, content SHA stays stable, review content digest reuses identical graph context, and changed graph output busts cache. |
| GitNexus/schema security boundary | Committed as a proposed maintainer contract in `docs/deep-regression-review.md`, including advisory-only graph context, stale/missing degradation, secret fail-closed behavior, and no release-safety claim. |
| Live review-run proof | Still an evidence gate, not a code defect. Local build/tests are green; current remote CI for this head is in progress. A redacted local-range/live review artifact should be attached before default enablement. |
| Maintainer approval | The proposed default-off boundary is now explicit and removable/editable by maintainers. |

## GitNexus In Plain English

GitNexus is an optional code graph/index. In this PR, ClawSweeper can use it for related-code hints:

- Which symbols or files are near the changed files?
- What other code paths may depend on this area?
- Is the local graph fresh, stale, missing, or unsafe to use?

It does not decide the review. It does not replace the PR diff. It does not guarantee release safety. It is a bounded advisory packet that helps ClawSweeper state what context it used and where confidence should be lower.

## Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["PR changes arrive"] --> B["Read GitHub diff and live checkout"]
  B --> C["Classify OpenClaw risk surface"]
  C --> D{"GitNexus enabled?"}
  D -- "No" --> E["Graph state = disabled"]
  D -- "Yes" --> F["Build advisory graph packet"]
  F --> G{"Packet safe and fresh enough?"}
  G -- "Yes" --> H["Record packet SHA and stable content SHA"]
  G -- "No" --> I["Degrade, omit, or fail closed"]
  E --> J["Compute review cache digest"]
  H --> J
  I --> J
  J --> K{"Cached report still valid?"}
  K -- "Yes" --> L["Reuse report"]
  K -- "No" --> M["Run fresh review"]
  M --> N["Render deepRegressionReview and proof boundary"]
  L --> N
```

## Validation

Local validation on `c96a27278952481a20ebb22538c5b0b2173d088a`:

```text
pnpm run build
node --test test/gitnexus-context.test.ts test/review-content-cache.test.ts test/decision-parser.test.ts
pnpm run format:check
pnpm run lint:src
git diff --check
```

Result:

```text
targeted tests: 46 pass, 0 fail
build: pass
format/lint/diff-check: pass
```

Prior broader validation on the previous head also passed:

```text
targeted tests: 155 pass, 0 fail
full unit suite: 707 pass, 0 fail
repair/router focused tests: 187 pass, 0 fail
format/lint/diff-check: pass
```

Remote validation for the new head is currently running in GitHub Actions.

Evidence packet: `/Volumes/LEXAR/Codex/evidence/clawsweeper-deep-regression/2026-07-09/issue-439/`

## Non-goals

- No OpenClaw runtime changes.
- No automatic merge or release gates by default.
- No public 1M-context claim.
- No release-safety or bug-free guarantee.
- No GitNexus auto-refresh in this PR.
- No embedded GitNexus index storage or embedding credentials.

## Proof Boundary

This prototype improves advisory review signal and confidence hygiene. It proves the seeded/cache/redaction/unit cases covered by tests and CI. It does not prove release readiness, bug-free releases, actual 1M-token context, or that GitNexus context is authoritative over the GitHub diff/checkout.

## Remaining Gate

Before default enablement, maintainers should review the committed boundary doc and collect a redacted live local-range or equivalent review-run artifact showing:

- default-off behavior;
- degraded GitNexus handling for missing/stale context;
- rendered `deepRegressionReview` output;
- packet SHA/content SHA/freshness fields with private details redacted.

Note: existing ClawSweeper bot comments created before the command-status cleanup fix require the bot/admin token to delete or minimize. The contributor token cannot rewrite those historical bot-owned comments, so this PR fixes the behavior going forward.
